data_section_full_text:
Sample and descriptive statistics
In this study, we examine public management earnings guidance of security analysts. The data are obtained from the First Call data base of “company-issued
guidelines”. Over our sample period of 1995 to 2001, the percentage of firms that
provided management guidance increases from 11 percent in 1995 to 31 percent in
2001, with an average of 22 percent over the entire sample period. We use the
number of firms with analyst forecasts in the First Call detailed analysts’ forecasts
file each year as the basis for calculating these percentages. For those firms that
provide management guidance, the maximum (minimum) number of quarters with
management guidance is 7 (1) out of the 28 sample quarters during the sample
period. On average, firms that provide management guidance do so in 1.67 out of
28 quarters.
Given that public management guidance is infrequent in our sample, we focus
on the factors that lead management to issue public guidance in a particular quarter

CAR Vol. 23 No. 3 (Fall 2006)

Expectations Management and Beatable Targets 603


and whether this guidance leads to beatable analyst forecast targets. Our sample
includes 22,190 firm-quarter observations by 1,673 firms that provided at least one
public quarterly management forecast between 1995 and 2001. We do not require a
sample firm to be in existence throughout the sample period, so our sampling procedure does not induce a material survivorship bias. Rather than using the fiscal
dates, we define the previous earnings announcement date as the start of the quarter and the current earnings announcement date as the end of the quarter.

If there is a management guidance event in a quarter, we record the date and
the attributes of the event. Pownall et al. (1993) find that the form of management
earnings guidance affects investors’ reactions to this guidance. Therefore, we code
the form of management guidance including point, range, “less than”, and “greater
than” open-ended forecasts to assess their impact on analyst forecast revisions. To
determine the earnings “information” contained in management guidance, we use
the exact values of point and open-ended management forecasts, and the midpoint
of range forecasts ~~.~~ <sup><u>3</u></sup>

The data set is designed so that all events happen within a given quarter. For
example, the date of the management earnings guidance must take place after the
announcement of the last quarter’s earnings and be related to earnings for the current quarter ~~.~~ <sup><u>4</u></sup> If a firm has provided more than one management forecast in a given
fiscal quarter, we keep only the first one. We merge these data with the First Call
data base of analyst estimates of earnings per share for the current fiscal quarter.
The date of each analyst forecast is also recorded. The sample of management and
analysts forecasts is then merged with the First Call “official actuals” file that contains the actual ex post earnings per share for the current fiscal quarter. Finally, the
data are merged with financial information from the COMPUSTAT data base to
obtain information on total assets and net income.
